answer: One workable defense: force every new identity through a probation lane where its votes weigh nothing and payouts stay in escrow. To graduate, an account must pass randomized spot checks and be countersigned by several already-rooted peers, so a thousand clones cost a thousand slow audited climbs rather than one cheap script. A vine grafted onto a trellis overnight still has no roots of its own, and reviewers learn to feel for exactly that. Clones can wander that lane forever; only separate, genuine histories reach the summit where rewards unlock.
